quote_text:
Immensely proud of the players for  what they put in. This was never going  
to be an easy couple of days for us. You could see how fatigued they were;  
you could see that we were starting to drop  like flies towards the end. If I had another  
few substitutions, I would have made them because  players were kind of out on their feet. But, you  
know, I thought we did what we set out to do in  the first half. You have an idea where you can try  
and get at the opposition, you've got an idea what  they're going to try and bring towards you. Maybe  
one or two surprises in their team selection,  but it didn't really change much in our mind.
And quite clearly, you could hear the atmosphere  in here at halftime — Motherwell supporters are  
over the moon, and Rangers supporters  are completely discontent with what  
they're seeing. Our message at halftime, and  this is my biggest frustration in the game,  
is that we come hard at the start of the  second half. And what I mean by that is  
that we show good reactions, that we try and  play the game in their half of the pitch,  
and we continue to try and play and get in  their face as much as we possibly can. And  
we didn’t. It took us just that wee bit too  long to get ourselves into the second half.
That’s twice it's happened — it happened  in the semi-final for us against them when  
we were 1-0 up, and it’s happened here  again today. Not good enough reactions  
inside the penalty area. But those are the  bits that I start to nitpick at for us to  
try and get better as a football  club. We hung in there in the end,  
of course we did. We put ourselves into  a position at the end where, at times,  
we’re collapsing too deep, at times we’re inviting  Rangers onto us. And again, for us to get better,  
we’re going to have to be able to handle this  type of schedule against that level of opposition.
That’s my biggest takeaway, but that’s what I want  for the football club, that’s what I want for the  
players, and I believe that they’ll grow and get  better if we can start to reach those heights.
Was that one that you feel you should have won? I think it’s fair to say. I think it’s fair to  
say. Again, I’m just left amused by,  one, the on-field decision. For me,  
it’s complete overprotection of a  goalkeeper. You have a look at it again;  
I would need to see whether the ball's in play or  not. But we’re seeing that the level of contact  
from Tony Watt justifies the foul. Then I would  start to argue, does the level of contact from  
Butland to also shove Tony Watt out of the way to  initiate it — does that then merit a penalty kick?  
Because that's where I think we’re getting to. I  think that’s the point we’re getting to, and the  
answer is no to either. It’s not a penalty,  but for me, it’s certainly not a free kick.
You know, Tony’s doing his job on the goalkeeper,  which you’re allowed to do. I think I saw  
an incident a few weeks ago — I think it was  Tottenham, and they scored direct from a corner.  
There’s a similar type of incident. And what do  they do down south? They have a quick look at it,  
they check it, and they give the goal.  And we carry on with the rest of the game.  
You know what I mean? So, it’s two people’s  interpretations, two different organizations’  
interpretations. And down there, they play on.  There’s no overprotection of the goalkeeper. But  
for some reason today, here, we’ve decided  that there was enough to merit a free kick.
I think it was late in the game,  eight to 10 minutes from the end. I  
imagine that would have been frustrating. Yeah, I’m tearing my hair out. And see,  
the point where I then start to get frustrated  — my frustration’s purely pent-up from this  
now going into the realms of five and six  weeks, seven weeks, with key decisions that  
I believe have gone against us. Some of them  have been confirmed as wrong. And we almost  
get a pat on the head and a “we got that  one wrong; we’ll move on to the next one.”
People need to realize how much I care about  this, how much the players care about it,  
and how much we’re fighting and scrapping to try  and do the absolute best we can. Now, I don’t  
blame referees or officials for outcomes of games  of football. But what I do ask for is the correct  
decision. I’m not asking for a rub of the green  here, but what I’m asking for is the correct call.
I’ll give you an example of that. Lennon Miller  goes into a tackle in the middle of the park,  
which results in an injury, believe it or not. But  for me, to my eye, it’s what I would call a hook  
tackle. You get side-on to the player, you go to  ground, which you’re allowed to do, you come out  
with the ball, which he does. He doesn’t come  through the player. And we actually check that  
for a red card. There’s a red card check within  that tackle. The referee instantly books him.
At this point, I start to become incredibly  frustrated because there are Rangers midfielders  
that have got away with four, five — I  think we’re even touching six — fouls  
in the middle of the park. Now, that’s  fine, that’s part and parcel of the game,  
but that affects and changes how  you play the game. You’re now on  
a knife-edge in the game. In this country,  that’s where it starts to boil over for me.
People might see that as a kind of insignificant  incident. It’s not. It’s not when you’re playing  
against that level of quality in players that can  do what they can do to you. And you have to try  
and gain every advantage. You’re just looking for  parity; you’re just looking for things to be very,  
very similar. And that Lennon Miller challenge  comes up as a perfectly good challenge. Fine,  
play on. But if it goes the other way and we start  mounting up four, five fouls, that’s generally  
persistent fouling, and this is how I see it.  But that wasn’t the case. That wasn’t the case.
And hence, I end up watching the  rest of the game in the stand. 
As usual, they’ll throw the book at  us. There’ll be another suspension  
to come and all the rest of it.  But I’m not going to change. I  
feel passionately about the game. I feel  passionately about this football club.  
And I feel passionately about what I see  on the pitch and calling it as I see it.
Can you explain why you got sent off? It was the first yellow for the Miller  
tackle. It was in reaction to that. I  was flabbergasted that it was given as  
a yellow card. And again, I’m a passionate  person. Sometimes you see a bit of emotion,  
sometimes you see that. But for that one,  genuinely, there was nothing abusive or  
anything of that nature towards the  fourth official or the linesman. I  
was just flabbergasted with the decision. I’ve  since seen it, and I still stand by what I said.
And then the second one, listen, let’s put it down  to a breakdown of communication between myself and  
the fourth official. And I’m probably not prepared  to go any further than that. But as I say,  
I’m the type of person that wears my heart on  my sleeve, and I’m not going to change for that.
Cheers.
title: Stuart Kettlewell Press Conference | Motherwell 2-2 Rangers
